title: Midday throughput lull for LexiAI dedicated pool during daily validation sweep causing temporary GPU attach shortfall
text:
Midday throughput lull for LexiAI dedicated pool during daily validation sweep causing temporary GPU attach shortfall

description:
Issue summary: LexiAI reported a ~30-40% sustained drop in steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) on their dedicated pool for ~18 minutes starting ~11:53 UTC on 2026-03-10. Impact: user-facing latency p50 increased from ~120ms to ~380ms and p99 spiked; some requests saw 5xx attach-timeouts. Environment: Dedicated capacity (capacity-id: ded-lexi-02) in us-west-2 running a mixed small/medium generation mix with batching enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Normal traffic to dedicated pool during midday window 2) At ~11:50 UTC the platform runs the daily model-validation sweep (internal scheduled job) which briefly reads multiple large checkpoints and triggers snapshotter activity across many hosts 3) Within 1–2 minutes GPUs in the LexiAI stripe experience attach delays and autoscaler changes 4) Throughput falls until snapshotter IO completes Observed logs/metrics: - NVMe queue depth on hosts servicing ded-lexi-02 spiked to >250 concurrent IO ops. - Kernel-level iowait rose from 2% to 45%. - GPU attach latency increased: median attach time 280ms -> 1.8s, 95th 3.1s. - Autoscaler observed short-lived burst in connection churn and reduced observed idle slots, triggered conservative downscale gating. - Snapshotter logs show overlapping GC/compaction jobs and a large checkpoint read at 11:50:12 UTC. Additional notes: Customer traffic itself is steady; spike correlates with platform schedule. Full metric dumps attached in investigation notes.

comments:
2026-03-10 - 12:05 - Priya Shah (Support): Received alert from LexiAI via console; opened ticket and started initial triage. Asked customer to confirm if they had any scheduled migrations (customer replied no).
2026-03-10 - 12:27 - Maya Chen (SRE): Observed NVMe io saturation on three hosts in the Lexi stripe. Temporarily pinned traffic away from worst hosts and notified infra to throttle snapshotter concurrency.
2026-03-10 - 13:15 - LexiAI (Customer): Confirmed degradations resolved after ~18 minutes, provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Asks for cause and mitigation for future midday windows.
2026-03-11 - 09:40 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced scenario in staging by running validation sweep with snapshotter concurrency set to 8. Observed attach delays and autoscaler hysteresis. Opened infra PR to add snapshotter backoff in heavy-io periods.
2026-03-12 - 10:02 - Priya Shah (Support): Updated customer with mitigation plan and temporary workaround; scheduled follow-up run with LexiAI for Wednesday maintenance window.
2026-03-13 - 16:45 - Aaron Patel (Platform Eng): Merged PR 1987 to rate-limit snapshotter read concurrency and added NVMe backlog circuit-breaker to scheduler. Monitoring in progress.

investigation_notes:
Timeline: 11:50 UTC snapshotter initiated a cross-host checkpoint read for model-validation sweep. NVMe bandwidth consumed by snapshot reads and compaction, iowait surged, CPU scheduled latencies increased and the serving runtime's allocator heartbeats jittered. Autoscaler interpreted jitter and short-lived connection churn as reduced effective capacity and delayed slot allocation, exacerbating attach latency. Key indicators: high nvme_io_wait and snapshotter log entries showing two compaction passes overlapping with reads. Hypothesis: snapshotter concurrency + compaction caused storage I/O saturation; serving runtime and autoscaler are sensitive to transient attach delays which trigger conservative fallback behavior leading to temporary GPU shortfall for the customer.

root_cause:
Concurrent snapshotter checkpoint reads and compaction tasks saturated host NVMe I/O during the validation sweep window. I/O saturation increased attach latency and caused autoscaler gating logic to avoid aggressive allocation, producing a transient GPU attach shortfall for LexiAI's dedicated stripe.

resolution:
Short-term: throttled snapshotter concurrency for the affected hosts and applied per-stripe IO priority so serving traffic gets NVMe priority. Re-routed LexiAI's traffic off the three worst hosts during remediation window. Long-term: merged infra change to add snapshotter backoff when host nvme queue depth > 150 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1987) and added a scheduler circuit-breaker to avoid compaction/read overlap. Also updated autoscaler to tolerate short attach latency spikes by smoothing attach latency signal over 30s window.

next_steps:
1) Run scheduled simulation of validation sweep in staging with new backoff and verify no attach latency spike (owner: Platform Eng, due: 2026-03-17). 2) Add a per-customer alert that correlates NVMe iowait with attach latency (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-20). 3) Work with LexiAI to move heavy validation jobs to a low-traffic maintenance window (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-18).

resolution_summary:
Merged rate-limit and backoff for snapshotter, added NVMe backlog circuit-breaker and autoscaler smoothing. Customer traffic restored to normal; monitoring shows no recurrence in 48h post-fix.

notes_for_postmortem:
Include reproducer steps for snapshotter compaction/read overlap and add a section on autoscaler sensitivity to attach latency. Consider adding explicit scheduling windows for model-validation jobs or isolated maintenance hosts for heavy IO operations.

customer_communication:
2026-03-11 - Sent preliminary RCA and immediate actions. 2026-03-13 - Sent final mitigation plan and timeline for staged infra rollout. Offered a post-incident call; customer accepted and scheduled for 2026-03-18.
